name: Light Sulphate Green
lede: Light Sulphate Green is a paler, bluer step off [[sulphate-green|Sulphate Green]], a vivid bluish green Ridgway plated in 1912 without naming any actual sulphate pigment.

sections.title: A modifier, not a chemical name
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[sulphate-green|Sulphate Green]]; the books mention sulphates giving dyers and pigment makers several green and blue colors, but none confirm this particular name came from one [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plates this lighter step at plate XIX, hue 39', tone b, and ISCC-NBS separately filed it in 1955 as block 163 [1]. Measured, it is noticeably lighter than its parent at a close chroma (lightness 74 against 60) [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[verditter-blue|Verditter Blue]], 4.7 units away, darker and duller, with [[medium-aquamarine|Medium Aquamarine]] close behind at 5.1, greener and more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale bluish green in 6 of 23,781 paintings (0.03 percent, as photographed), rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 1825, 87 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.named_after: a descriptive modifier: light + Sulphate Green
origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature
